checkpoints.question: Factory registration and licences (Shops & Establishments / Factories Act) are valid and up to date.
Employment contracts/appointment letters issued to all employees as per law.
Standing Orders or Employee Handbook available, displayed, and communicated.
Age proof documents maintained for all workers (Aadhaar, birth certificate, school records).
No child labour policy in place and signed by management.
Workmen compensation / ESIC registration and compliance verified.
PF registration and compliance – Forms, challans, and employee enrolments.
Contractor compliance documents (RC, labour licence, wage registers) verified monthly.
Transparent recruitment process without discrimination or unfair fees.
Induction training conducted and recorded for all new hires.
Equal opportunity policy implemented (gender, caste, religion, disability).
No withholding of original documents (Aadhaar, certificates, bank cards).
No forced labour – freedom to resign, no deposits, no coercion.
Use of temporary/contract labour complies with the Contract Labour Act.
Wage structure complies with State Minimum Wages (skilled, semi-skilled categories).
Timely payment of wages (within 7th or 10th as applicable).
Overtime wages paid at double rate as per the Factories Act.
Accurate payroll records – attendance, deductions, hours worked.
Statutory deductions (PF, ESIC, PT) correctly calculated and deposited.
Payslips issued with all details of earnings and deductions.
No illegal deductions (production loss, fines without legal process).
Working hours comply with law (48 hrs/week, 9 hrs/day).
Overtime limits follow legal norms (max 50–60 hrs/month depending on state).
Weekly off provided every 7th day.
Accurate timekeeping system (biometric/manual attendance).
Breaks provided as per law (rest intervals, lunch breaks).
Written HR policies (leave, discipline, harassment, grievance) are communicated.
POSH Committee formed as per the Sexual Harassment Act; training conducted.
Grievance mechanism available (suggestion boxes, hotline, HR contact).
Disciplinary procedures fair, documented, and non-abusive.
Union or worker committee meetings recorded.
Worker welfare amenities (drinking water, toilets, dining area) adequate and hygienic.
Medical room / first-aid boxes maintained with trained first-aiders.
Personal protective equipment (PPE) issued and records maintained.
Fire safety training and mock drills documented for all staff.
Accident records & investigation reports maintained.
Maternity benefits provided (MB Act compliance, leave records).
Crèche facility provided if applicable (30 or more women workers).
Crèche Staff is appointed
Daily attendence register is maintained in the Crèche facility.
Consent to Establish (CTE) / Consent to Operate (CTO) from the Pollution Control Board is valid.
Hazardous Waste Authorization (if applicable) maintained and compliant.
Air & Water pollution monitoring reports available and within permissible limits.
DG set emission and noise certificates updated.
Stack/effluent monitoring records maintained and submitted to authorities as required.
Waste segregation system implemented (hazardous, recyclable, general waste).
E-waste collection & disposal through authorized recyclers.
Chemical storage compliant with MSDS guidelines and labelled properly.
Spill control kits available near chemical handling areas.
Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP/STP) functional with logbooks maintained.
Water conservation measures implemented (metering, leak prevention).
Energy conservation practices documented (LED, efficient motors).
Record of waste disposal manifests (Form 10 for hazardous waste).
Fire extinguishers of appropriate types installed, serviced, and tagged.
Fire hydrant system/sprinklers maintained and pressure-tested.
Emergency exits unlocked, well-marked, illuminated, and unobstructed.
Fire alarm system functional with monitoring records.
Mock drills conducted and documented (twice/year recommended).
Trained fire wardens and emergency response team appointed.
Machine safety guards installed on all sewing/fabric cutting/finishing equipment.
Needle guard & eye guard present on sewing machines.
Lockout–Tagout (LOTO) procedure implemented for maintenance.
Electrical panels properly labelled, insulated, and with no exposed wires.
Safe storage of LPG/boilers/compressors with valid certificates.
Noise level monitoring conducted in high-noise areas.
Ventilation and lighting adequate in all work areas.
Housekeeping maintained – no debris, obstructed aisles, or blocked access.
Emergency evacuation plan displayed on all floors.
Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) available for all chemicals.
Chemical handling training provided to workers.
Bunded storage areas for chemicals and oils to prevent spills.
Proper labelling of all containers (hazard symbols, contents).
First-aid eyewash stations and showers available where chemicals are used.
First-aid boxes adequately stocked and accessible.
Medical room or tie-up with registered medical practitioner available as per law.
Accident & near-miss records maintained and investigated.
PPE distribution and usage monitored (masks, gloves, earplugs, safety shoes).
SOP for PPE is maintained
SOP for PPE is updated as per requirements
Periodic health check-ups conducted for workers as required by law.
Workstations arranged ergonomically (proper seating, adjustable chairs, footrests).
Aisles and evacuation routes clearly marked and unobstructed.
Emergency exits unlocked during working hours.
Sufficient ventilation (fans, exhaust, cross-ventilation, HVAC where required).
Adequate lighting across sewing, cutting, finishing, and packing areas.
Machine guards (needle guards, belt guards, cutting machine guards) installed and functional.
Sharp tool management (scissors, cutters issued & logged).
Fabric cutting tables maintained safely with no electrical hazards.
Ironing and steam stations have insulated pipes and emergency shut-offs.
Noise control measures in high-noise machinery areas.
Mandatory PPE use (masks, gloves, aprons, safety shoes where applicable).
No loose clothing or accessories near moving machinery.
Safe load handling practices followed for lifting and material movement.
Chemical usage (spot cleaning) done with proper ventilation and PPE.
Fire extinguishers accessible and workers trained to use them.
Production targets not set at levels that encourage unsafe speed or excessive overtime.
Supervisor conduct training completed and documented.
Material movement safe and organized (trolleys used; no overloading).
Needle policy implemented (tracking, breakage logs, metal detection where required).
Machine maintenance logs updated (preventive maintenance schedule followed).
Calibration of critical equipment (scales, metal detectors, cutters) maintained.
Work-in-progress (WIP) areas organized to avoid clutter and fire risks.
Evacuation diagrams displayed at production floor entry/exit points.
Fire alarm points accessible with workers trained on their use.
Smoke detectors / sprinklers functional where installed.
Fire drills participation from production staff is recorded.
Quality checkpoints clearly defined (end-line, inline QA).
Rework area separated and safely organized.
Use of safe chemicals only (spot cleaning chemicals approved by EHS team).
Packaging materials stored properly to avoid fire hazards.
Production records accurate. No double books.
Buyer Code of Conduct displayed & communicated to production staff.
Production floors have adequate material flow mapping to prevent congestion or cross-traffic between cutting, sewing, and finishing sections.
Bottleneck areas identified and decongested to avoid crowding and unsafe working conditions.
Operators trained on machine start-up/shut-down procedures, and training logs maintained.
Visual management boards (output, defects, safety alerts) displayed and updated daily.
No sitting on tables, fabric bundles, or unsafe surfaces—clear discipline observed on the floor.
Fans and overhead fixtures firmly secured with routine safety inspections.
Electrical cords, plug points, and extension boards on the floor kept away from walkways and heat sources.
Pressing/steam stations equipped with drip trays and insulated flooring to prevent slips or burns.
